SUBJECTIVE: Rosa Delgado returns for diabetes follow-up. She reports increased thirst and nocturia, suggestive of hyperglycemia. She denies stomach upset with metformin and reports good adherence, taking it with breakfast and dinner. She has recently started walking every evening. She requests a refill of metformin as she is nearly out.
OBJECTIVE: Vitals: BP 128/82 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98%, Temp 36.7 C. Labs from 2026-09-15 show HbA1c 7.4% and eGFR 78 mL/min. Patient is a 58-year-old female with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Allergy: penicillin (rash).
ASSESSMENT: 1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: HbA1c is 7.4%, above the target of <7.0% [guide:type-2-diabetes-followup@3#1]. Symptoms of polyuria and polydipsia are present. The rise from 7.1% is modest. Per guidelines, an HbA1c between 7.0-7.9% warrants review of diet and activity before intensification [guide:type-2-diabetes-followup@3#1]. Renal function is stable (eGFR 78 mL/min), permitting continued metformin use [guide:type-2-diabetes-followup@3#2].
2. Hypertension: Current BP 128/82 mmHg is at target. Previous elevated readings were not confirmed; this visit's reading is at target [guide:hypertension-followup@4#1].
PLAN: 1. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily. Refill queued as the dose is unchanged, adherence is confirmed, and eGFR >45 mL/min [guide:metformin-prescribing@2#2].
2. Reinforce lifestyle modifications: patient is already walking; advised to continue carbohydrate monitoring.
3. Repeat HbA1c in 3 months to assess response to lifestyle measures, given current HbA1c is <8.0% [guide:type-2-diabetes-followup@3#1].
4. BP monitoring at home.
